newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen up by Tokyo noon on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen up by Tokyo noon on short-covering.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen contract rose by Tokyo midday on Monday due to demand for hedging and short-covering, traders said.
"Major long-term and city banks received fixed interest rates in various maturities (in the swap market), inducing hedge purchases in the euroyen market," said a trader at a city bank.
The March was at 98.91 at Tokyo noon, up from Friday's 98.86 settlement.
The key three-year IRS (interest rate swap) was quoted at 1.47/51 percent, down sharply from 1.53/57 percent on Friday.
The five year IRS was quoted at 2.00/04 percent, down from 2.04/08 percent on Friday.
Some said that despite March's upswing, its buoyancy from the current level was limited due to profit-taking sales demand accumulated since last week.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) drained 300 billion yen from the money market through its regular operation at 0020 GMT, leaving the market with a 270 billion yen surplus.
The central bank has been providing ample liquidity to the market in a bid to offset upward pressure on rates typically seen at the end of the month, traders said.
